seo_title: Heartware Network Case Study: Volunteer Brand Voice | SOMIN
description: Fyreflyz used SOMIN to read 1,230 posts for Heartware Network: 87.9% of its posts used the category's two voices, and it had never run a paid placement.
eyebrow: Agency case study · Youth volunteering · Singapore
h1: Heartware puts 87.9% of its posts in two voices, and nobody owns a third
lede: Fyreflyz used SOMIN to read 1,230 posts from Heartware Network and its category. 87.9% of Heartware's posts used two voices, it ran no paid placements, and its own hypothesis failed.
meta_line: A SOMIN agency pitch · 1 May to 19 Aug 2026 · Singapore · Youth 14 to 35

challenge.title: Heartware holds 20.2% of category voice but sounds like the rest
challenge.body: Heartware Network trails only the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore, yet 116 of its 132 posts use The Sage or The Caregiver voice, like most of the category.

approach.title: 1,230 posts in three cohorts and one tested hypothesis
points: Read 132 Heartware posts against six competitors (522) and seven youth-sector organisations (576).
Tagged archetype, tone, content type, audience and captions.
Tested the client hypothesis and checked 12 months of paid ads.
Drew on 20 SOMIN studies in two workspaces.

findings_title: Heartware's two voices, failed hypothesis and Facebook gap

findings.title: 85.2% of competitor and youth-sector posts use two voices
findings.body: They are The Sage and The Caregiver, across 1,098 posts. Heartware is at 87.9%, with a cohort-low 4.5% in Creator, Explorer or Jester.

findings.title: Skill-based volunteering is not whitespace
findings.body: Heartware is at 25.0%, competitors at 28.2%. Only 1 of 9 territories, restoring self-worth and dignity, clears the test.

findings.title: One recap: 337 likes on Instagram, 0 on Facebook
findings.body: The copy was identical. Facebook takes 22% of output at 3.1 engagements per post, against 155.1 on Instagram.

delivered.title: An SGD 120,000 media plan, a Q4 calendar and 54 creatives
points: Three pillars: Unfiltered Stories, Level Up Your Impact and Micro-MAD Moments
39 dated Q4 slots, three a week, none for Facebook
A twelve-month plan, an SGD 33,000 Q4 pilot and three-case KPI projections
Creatives across pillars and funnel stages, plus a measurement plan

quote.text: Everyone bought the lectern and the safety net. Nobody bought the workbench.

outcome.title: Heartware's plan: 45% of budget behind volunteer-authored stories
outcome.body: Another 40% backs proof of what named young people can now do. Micro-MAD Moments is a capped SGD 12,000 test with a public readout on 31 Dec 2026.

faq.q: What was wrong with the client's hypothesis?
faq.a: Heartware assumed skill-based volunteering was open ground. It was not, so the pillar now rests on proof of what volunteers can do.

faq.q: Why does Facebook get no budget line?
faq.a: Identical creative scored 337 likes on Instagram and 0 on Facebook. Meta is bought as one Instagram-optimised pool; Facebook takes spill only.

faq.q: How reliable are the sign-up projections?
faq.a: They are modelled in three cases. The plan uses 520 to 2,792 YouthBank sign-ups in 12 months; the 12,061 stretch case is a ceiling above onboarding capacity.
